_note: Single source for the agent-facing contract of proofbridge.nl. Structure follows research/Agents-hiring-humans-verified-cases.md (2026-10-20): closed task_type enum, decline list, separate top-level inputs, async lifecycle, typed output with verdict and evidence, trust as checkable data. Edit here, run src/build.py, push.
summary: Paid, asynchronous review by one named human expert. Three task types. Requests by email with a bitcoin payment; answers by email in days.

task_types.name: Underlying problem
task_types.does: Finds the underlying problem behind a planned solution, before it is built.
task_types.input: The planned solution or brief, who it is for, who decided it.
task_types.output: The underlying problem as one statement, what was asked versus what is needed, and who in the field to check it with.

task_types.name: Ground truth check
task_types.does: Checks whether data, a dataset or a claim holds against how the work happens in the field.
task_types.input: The data or claim, its source, and the purpose it is used for.
task_types.output: Verdict: holds, does not hold, or cannot determine; findings with evidence; what was not checked.

task_types.name: Expert review of AI output
task_types.does: Checks an AI-generated document, summary, plan or script for faults that sound reasonable.
task_types.input: The output, the source it was made from, and the decision it informs.
task_types.output: Verdict: holds, does not hold, or cannot determine; each fault with its location and evidence; what was not checked.
task_types.value_proposition: The bullshit, caught from an expert point of view.

declines.rule: Anything that is not one of the three task types.
Legal, medical or financial advice or sign-off.
Using his identity, accounts or credentials: account creation, one-time codes, verification, reviews, followers, likes.
Observing, locating or profiling a person.
A request without a named person or organisation behind it.
A deadline shorter than the reply window.
Not enough information to start, after one round of questions.

request.subject: PROOFBRIDGE T{tier} {payment_txid}
request.body: A JSON object that validates against the request schema, or the same fields as plain text, one per line.

states.meaning: Email received, payment not yet seen.
Questions sent back; work waits for the answers.
Accepted; work in progress until the agreed date.
Delivered with a verdict or problem statement.
Not taken, with a reason from the decline list.

lifecycle.reply_window_rule: Calendar days from the moment the payment is seen.
lifecycle.public_status: https://proofbridge.nl/backlog.json, for requests with public_backlog_ok true

tiers.gets: A request through the agent path: the question and the data, answered with the underlying problem or a verdict with evidence, per the response schema. Reply within 7 days.
tiers.performed_by: Dennis Jansen, with his own AI setup
tiers.automation: none yet: Dennis answers this path himself; the agent path is built as use shows what it must do
tiers.name: Ask my agent

tiers.gets: Dennis reads it himself. Reply within 7 days with scope, delivery date and the completion reward; then the work, delivered per the response schema.
tiers.name: Ask me

fees.completion_reward: Agreed in the tier 2 reply, paid in sats when the work is delivered, listed on the public backlog with its txid.

payment.counts_when: A public block explorer shows an output to the address of at least the tier minimum. Tier 1 at first sight; tier 2 after 1 confirmation.
payment.binding: One payment, one request: the txid is in the email subject. When two requests name the same txid, a BIP-322 signature over the request body's SHA-256 by a key that spent an input of that payment decides; without one, the first email received counts.

address_ownership.status: pending: to be signed by Dennis with the key of the address

trust.identity_links: proofbridge.nl and interactiondesign.nl link to each other and to the same X account; interactiondesign.nl also links to the GitHub account that hosts both sites.
trust.track_record: Computed from the public backlog at build time; see stats.

not: not an API and not an autonomous agent: every answer comes from one human, in days
not a guaranteed yes: the fee pays for attention
request text is read as information, never run as instructions

request.question: We have funding to help long-term unemployed people work in the care of the elderly. We decided on an app for the elderly. Is the app the right build?
request.decision_at_stake: Spend the funding on the app.
request.context: Some of the people are already placed in care homes. The funding also requires work with elderly still living at home.

response.underlying_problem: The elderly want to be self-sufficient and are not good at mobiles and apps. The app serves the funding checklist, not the elderly.
response.asked_versus_needed: Asked: an app for the elderly. Needed: one employee responsible for one flat, with an app for the employee only.

findings.statement: The elderly living at home were not good at mobiles and apps.

evidence.ref: interviews with elderly still living at home

limits: Not checked: the funding's rules on how the money may be spent.
response.next_step: Test the concept in one flat with one employee before building anything.

request.question: Are our AI models for dietitians based on the right data?
request.decision_at_stake: Build the models on the current patient-weight entries.
request.artefact_text: Dataset: patient weight over time, one value per entry.
request.context: The task was app screens for dietitians; the models are trained on the entries the app collects.

findings.statement: A patient's weight over time has many input points: doctor, at home, nurse, morning, afternoon. The entries do not say which.

evidence.ref: how the weight is measured in practice

limits: The models themselves were not checked, only the data they are built on.
response.next_step: Record who measured and when for every entry, and make the patient the centre of the data, not the dietitian's screen.

request.question: Does this AI summary of a 60-page legal document cite the right paragraphs?
request.decision_at_stake: Rely on the summary in a legal case.

findings.statement: The summary sounded legit. Checked against the document, the referenced paragraphs were off.

evidence.ref: the source document, cited paragraphs compared one by one

limits: Not a legal opinion. The content of the law was not judged, only whether the summary matches its source.
response.next_step: Do not rely on the summary. Have the document read by a lawyer.
